verification_report.summary:
The complete proof is correct under the expressly accepted prerequisites. All deductions were checked in textual order, including both concluding paragraphs. No critical errors or gaps were found.

Bigness supplies a>0 with theta-a h pseudoeffective, so monotonicity and homogeneity give lambda_mu(theta)>=a lambda_mu(h)>0. For pseudoeffective nonbig theta, the accepted threshold criterion gives kappa_h(theta)=0. A minimizing sequence of ratios exists by the definition of infimum. For n>=2, scaling each metric eta_j by A_h(eta_j)^(-1/(n-1)) preserves the Gauduchon condition and both ratios, gives A_h=1, and makes A_theta tend to zero. The defining inequality 0<D_mu(gamma_j)<=A_theta(gamma_j)/lambda_mu(theta) then proves collapse for every sequence in part 2.

The conditional inequality is valid: pseudoeffectivity ensures lambda_mu(theta)>=0; when it is positive, the denominator liminf bound and convergence of A_theta give kappa_h(theta)>=delta lambda_mu(theta). When lambda_mu(theta)=0, the conclusion is simply kappa_h(theta)>=0. No convergence of D_mu or interchange of infimum and limit is required. Applying the basic inequality to h gives the stated uniform upper bound, without supplying a lower bound.

For n=1, gamma^0=1 and D_mu=integral mu=1, so lambda_mu(theta)=integral theta and kappa_h(theta)=(integral theta)/(integral h). Positivity and bigness are therefore equivalent. Scaling cannot impose A_h=1 in this dimension unless integral h already equals one; the proof correctly restricts its normalization construction to n>=2, and part 3 remains valid whenever its hypotheses hold.

The argument uses no closedness, bounded mass property, global lower mass bound, compactness of the metric space, or attainment by a minimizing metric. It does not prove the unconditional converse in higher dimensions. All reference applications match the accepted premises; no new external-paper citation requires checking.
